title: Secure suggester apply workflow for batching & caching recommendations (RBAC + chronicle audit)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
We are building a controlled 'suggester -> apply' pipeline that turns automated batching and KV caching recommendations into safe runtime config changes. The goal is to let the optimization engine propose config deltas (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization knobs) and have an auditable, RBAC-gated path for those to be applied and, if needed, rolled back automatically. This ticket scopes the server-side workflow, change record format (chronicle), approval matrix, and forensic logging hooks required by Compliance and Support.

Background: The suggester service has produced reliable recommendations in staging for weeks; ops wants a way to reduce token cost by autonomously applying low-risk changes while ensuring operators and auditors can trace, review, and revert changes quickly. We must balance velocity (auto-apply low-risk recommendations) with governance (explicit approval for high-impact changes).

Non-goals: this ticket does not change model selection or add new inference kernels. It also does not expand the suggester's rule language — only the change execution and audit surface.

Constraints: audited events must be immutable, include pre/post config diffs and evidence (metric snapshots), and be exportable to our SIEM. RBAC must map to existing org roles (engineer, infra-owner, security-reviewer, compliance). Changes applied by automation must be labeled with policy provenance and revert trigger conditions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A change record (chronicle) is written for every suggester proposal containing: proposer ID, proposal hash, diff, metric snapshot, risk score, and policy tag.
A2: RBAC checks occur before any non-zero-risk change apply; low-risk (score <= 0.2) can be auto-applied by the 'suggester-bot' service if org policy allows.
A3: All apply and rollback actions are logged to the immutable audit stream and are searchable in Console (per-route and per-model views) within 30s.

A4: Automatic rollback triggers are implemented and tested (regression in p50 latency > 10% OR error rate increase > 0.5%) and can be overridden only by an infra-owner with 'emergency-apply' privilege.
A5: An operator can review, approve, or block pending proposals via Console and the action is recorded with timestamp, approver, and justification.
A6: Compliance export: chronicles can be exported as a JSONL archive with chained signatures for external audit.
A7: Unit and integration tests cover RBAC checks, chronicle integrity, and rollback orchestration (CI gate).
A8: A runbook with playbook steps for manual rollback and escalation is added to Confluence and linked in the chronicle entries.
A9: No change is applied without a chronicle entry and corresponding metric snapshot attached.
A10: Performance: adding the chronicle write and RBAC check increases tail apply latency by no more than 50ms in the happy path.
A11: Security review sign-off attached to the PR before merge (security_review_required=true).

decision: Adopt a two-tier policy: auto-apply for score <= 0.2 with 'suggester-bot' identity; for 0.2 < score <= 0.7 require one infra-owner approval; score > 0.7 require security + compliance approval. All actions must write a chronicle entry and propagate to SIEM. Auto-applies get a 24h watch window during which regression triggers auto-rollback.
rollback_plan: If p50 latency regression > 10% or error-rate bump > 0.5% within 24h -> orchestrator triggers immediate rollback using stored pre-apply snapshot.
Operators can trigger manual rollback from Console; action records approver and justification.
Emergency-apply/override requires infra-owner role with emergency token and is logged to chronicle with separate escalation path.
Rollback runs through the same chronicle recording pipeline so every revert is also auditable and exportable.
implementation_notes: Chronicle schema v1: fields = proposal_id, proposer, proposal_hash, diff, pre_metrics, post_metrics, risk_score, policy_version, signatures, apply_time, revert_time, evidence_links
Use existing Kinesis audit stream and add 'chronicle' topic with immutability guarantees (SSE + write-once bucket design).
RBAC mapping: reuse org roles in IAM; introduce 'suggester-bot' service account with scoped permissions to call apply endpoint only when policy allows.
Make signatures verifiable: sign with platform HSM key, include key_id in chronicle entry. Work with Security to rotate keys quarterly.
Console: surface pending proposals table, risk_score, metric delta preview, approve/deny buttons, and single-click rollback for last 24h auto-applies.
Testing: simulate noisy traffic to validate rollback triggers and ensure no false positives for p50 fluctuations.
risks: False positive regressions could cause unnecessary rollbacks and cost churn — mitigate by conservative thresholds and smoothing metrics.
Privilege escalation if service account permissions are too broad — mitigate with least-privilege vectors and code review of apply endpoint.
Loss of audit data if chronicle publishing fails — implement retry + dead-lettering and monitor publish success rates.
Operational confusion if Console UI does not clearly distinguish auto-applies from human-applies — ensure UI badges and filters.
